grades.quote: This is potentially dangerous because the condition being waited for may not be true. However, xv6 calls to sleep are always wrapped in a while loop that re-tests the condition after sleep returns.
grades.reason: Directly explains why the wait (sleep) is wrapped in a while loop: a wakeup (e.g., from kill) can return the sleeper when the awaited condition is not true, so the loop re-tests the condition after sleep returns.

grades.quote: If there are more than one of them, they will all try to acquire the condition lock and re-check the condition; in many cases only one will be able to do anything useful (e.g., read all the data waiting in a pipe).
grades.reason: Gives supporting reasons for re-checking the condition after waking: wakeup wakes all waiters and only one may find the condition true, and sleepers can be woken before the awaited event happens. It does not explicitly state the while-loop idiom.
Covers concurrency in device drivers and interrupt handlers. It says nothing about condition-variable waits or re-testing a condition in a while loop.
Covers sleep-locks versus spinlocks. It does not explain why condition waits belong in a while loop.
